narrative_purpose: Returns the close to Jodie Holt's overlooked laboratory error and makes the contamination mechanism visible: smoke from one casual cigarette can cross into living plant samples.
subject: A genetics laboratory bench with a lit cigarette abandoned in a shallow metal dish at the far left, a thin plume of smoke drifting horizontally across the frame. In the center, an open sterile plant-culture dish contains several small green leaf cuttings in clear gel. At the smoke front, hundreds of tiny rod-shaped particles travel with the haze and settle onto the exposed leaf tissue. At the far right, a sealed identical culture dish remains clear and untouched for comparison. No person is present.
scene: A sober Earth laboratory after hours, stainless work surface and dark out-of-focus equipment behind, the careless contamination event isolated on the bench.
camera: Bench-height close side view following the smoke from cigarette to open culture dish to sealed control dish.
light: Cool clinical overhead light, with the cigarette ember as the only scarce warm accent and a faint cyan edge on the clean glassware.
palette: Cool clinical greys and deep indigo shadow, living green leaf tissue, restrained ember amber only at the cigarette tip.
style: Painterly scientific incident plate, precise and understated, not sensational.
detail_level: Crisp cigarette ember, smoke-borne particles, exposed leaf tissue and sealed control; background equipment soft and unreadable.
composition: A left-to-right contamination path with open negative space above the cigarette, open dish and sealed dish for later callouts.
consistency_notes: This is an Earth genetics lab, not Pandora. The teaching relationship must be literal: smoke and particles reach the open plant sample while the sealed control remains untouched.
negative_prompt: no text, no brand marks, no people smoking, no fire beyond one small ember, no gore, no photographic or glossy 3D-render look, no clutter obscuring the dishes
